conflicts.why: Both select architecture/dependencies/layer-direction: CA-DEP-001 checks every layer and FCIS-DEP-001 only the core layer. Resolving deps.layers to CA-DEP-001 keeps the wider check, which still covers the core.

relations.why: Both select architecture/dependencies/layer-direction: CA-DEP-001 checks every layer and FCIS-DEP-001 only the core layer, so the core check is contained in the wider one.
relations.settle: Resolve deps.layers to architecture/CA-DEP-001; the core-layer check stays covered.

relations.why: Both check imports from core-layer files against the preset layers, so one forbidden edge is reported twice.
relations.settle: Keep one of them: both run the same layer-edge evaluation on the core layer.

source.locator: the functional core and imperative shell section
source.paraphrase: The shell calls the core. The core must not depend on the shell that performs external effects.

invariants.why: A local shell import can hide external effects even when the core imports no I/O package directly.
invariants.fixHint: Pass the required values or a narrow collaborator from the shell. Declare any stable data or port layer explicitly in the preset's layer map.
invariants.avoid: Type-only imports, path aliases and local re-export chains retain the dependency. Unresolved dependencies cannot prove a permitted edge. This graph check does not prove that every implementation is pure or determine module ownership.

relations.why: Both deny pg, mysql2, mongodb and @prisma/client in the core layer, so one import of those packages is reported twice.
relations.settle: Keep both when each list is wanted; to report once, drop the shared packages from one alias with a packages override.

source.locator: the functional core and imperative shell section
source.paraphrase: Keep decisions in a core of pure functions over plain values, and push every interaction with the outside world, such as files, network and processes, out to a thin shell.

invariants.why: A core that performs I/O cannot be tested with plain values and hides its effects from its callers.
invariants.fixHint: Let the shell do the I/O and pass the resulting values into core functions; the core returns values that describe what the shell must do.
invariants.avoid: Importing the same module with a node: prefix, through a subpath such as fs/promises, as a type-only import or through a local re-export.

relations.why: Both report Date.now() and new Date() in domain files of the core layer, so one clock read is reported twice.
relations.settle: FCIS-IO-002 also covers randomness and the environment; turn MAINT-CLOCK-001 off when the core layer is the domain.

relations.why: Both flag crypto randomness and performance.now() when domain, entity, or use-case folders belong to the core layer.
relations.settle: Keep one active or turn architecture/ARCH-EFF-002 off when FCIS-IO-002 covers the core layer.

source.locator: ch. 3, Distinguishing actions, calculations, and data
source.paraphrase: Calculations turn equal inputs into equal outputs every time; code whose result depends on the moment it runs or on how many times it runs, like reading the clock or a random number, is an action.

invariants.why: Reading the clock, randomness, the environment or the network makes the core nondeterministic, so its results cannot be reproduced in a test.
invariants.fixHint: Read the time, random values and configuration in the shell and pass them to the core as parameters.
invariants.avoid: Aliasing or destructuring the global, bracket access, going through globalThis, constructing a Date without arguments, or switching to Temporal, node:crypto, Bun, Deno, import.meta.env or the global fetch.
